title: Stained In Red And Black
paragraphs: “Ugh… so we have to decipher that writing ourselves?”
“That’s correct. But if it’s in the official language of Melromarc, I can transcribe a translation for you. It’s something I learned from Father in the first world.”
“Wait, we’re in Siltvelt right now, right? And if we’re heading to Faubrey too, won’t the language be different?”
“Indeed. I can’t read Siltvelt’s script either.”
Father and the others let out exasperated sighs.
What’s wrong now?
“You pulled all of that off without even understanding anything beyond Melromarc’s language!?”
“You can’t even go there anymore! Why bother learning their writing!?”
“I wouldn’t say I can’t go. If necessary, I can always buy some magic books while I’m there.”
No big deal. I’m already planning to head there to purchase my precious Filo-tan from the monster trader anyway.
“Wow… he’s really planning to go back like it’s nothing.”
“To be so shameless after everything that happened… this is the very definition of thick-skinned.”
“The truth is, no one would dare lay a hand on him out of sheer fear of his strength. In a way… that’s what being a hero is.”
Father and the others let out deep sighs of resignation. That’s right.
I am a hero who fights for true peace alongside Father and Filo-tan… and I am also the Love Hunter!
“That said, when it comes to magic, learning from books leads to a deeper understanding. You can use magic orbs to cast spells instantly, but…”
“Which one is more expensive?”
“Books, I’d assume?”
“No, wouldn’t the easier method be pricier?”
“Éclair would probably know best, but… she’s completely out of it right now, so we can’t ask her.”
Father glanced briefly at Éclair before turning to me with an exasperated look. As expected, she was still completely drained, looking utterly defeated.
“Just to add, after kicking Father out on false charges, Melromarc oh-so-generously provided us heroes with magic orbs for free.”
“So they really did intend to exclude Naofumi entirely.”
“We fell for the setup, got swept along, and just rode the wave without questioning anything.”
“Perhaps we should raid them and take the magic orbs back?”
“Yeah, no. That’s not happening, Motoyasu.”
Father promptly shut down my idea.
“But considering the importance of magic acquisition, sending Motoyasu might actually…”
“You know, there’s a protagonist who once said, ‘Criminals have no human rights.’”

“No, no… if we keep treating everything like a game and just ignore common sense, even if we save this world, we’ll have no place in it afterward. Worse, if we return home, we might still think we can solve everything with force.”
“That’s a fair point. I was already planning to cut ties with that country, so maybe it’s better to just forget about them entirely.”
“It’s already too late for that, but you know what they say—leave without making a mess.”
“You definitely left a mess. A big one.”
It’s good to see them getting along. Compared to the previous loops, Ren and Itsuki are much more reasonable this time.
“So, Motoyasu, we just need to stick to the enhancement methods we each know, right?”
“Yes, the Four Saints’ enhancement methods are all fine.”
“Why are you emphasizing ‘Four Saints’ so much? You’re making it sound like there are others.”
“There are, but for now, it’s more important to focus on mastering the ones available to you.”
At my words, Father and the others looked at me with mild exasperation.
“With this many enhancement methods, it makes sense that there would be even more out there.”
“At this point, we just have to believe in everything and move forward. If we keep doubting, we’ll be left behind—Motoyasu has already demonstrated that much.”
“Still, as a Shield Hero with no attack power, I doubt I’ll really feel much stronger…”
“That might be why our future selves didn’t believe in it.”

As they talked, Father and the others continued discussing the various enhancement methods. At one point, Father seemed flustered when we brought up weapon drops and weapon copying. He kept saying, “Those exist!?” over and over. He probably didn’t know about them. In the last loop and the one before that, I personally taught him all this one-on-one, so he never had to ask.
“Still… everything’s scattered all over the place, huh?”
“That said, some of them seem pretty similar to each other.”
“Yeah. Like ore-based enhancements—you’ve got the risk-free version with a cap, and the high-risk version without one. Easy to mix up.”
“With all these enhancement methods, mine feels so dull it might as well not even exist.”

Oh yeah, there was something called Job Levels, wasn’t there? That’s not something to underestimate. They’re actually necessary for learning skills and abilities—if you neglect them, you’ll regret it later.
“Ideally, we’d move straight into practicing these enhancements, but we don’t have the materials for anything.”
“…Yeah, that’s true. But at least we got to learn about them before testing them out.”
“The system is complicated, but it’s not impossible to learn. I’m a pretty hardcore gamer myself, so I can just relate things to similar mechanics in other games.”
Father subtly offers his support.
“Indeed. Before being transported here, Father was an executive in the third-ranked guild on his game server.”
“You sure know a lot. So you really are from the future, huh?”

His tone is softening bit by bit. At first, he acted all wary and skeptical, but once he realizes how sincere we are, his words gradually become kinder. Father is easy to read like that. I can feel that he’s starting to trust us. He really is like a mirror reflecting the world around him. When people treat him kindly, he becomes kind. When people are harsh, he responds in kind. The lively, easygoing side of him is nice too, but… it must have been tough for him.
“Third place on a server? That sounds pretty hard to achieve.”

“It’s not that difficult. You just gather promising players among the people you meet, invite rising talents to join your hunts, and manage those who aren’t motivated properly… In some games, it’s called a fortress, in others, it’s a raid? There’s always a standard strategy for those things.”
“Just hearing that makes it sound really complicated.”
Ren’s gaze sharpened slightly.
Was that… jealousy? Since Ren has a strong solo-player mindset, it makes sense that he’d react that way.

“Now that I think about it, Ren mentioned something in the first world. He said he had acquaintances who resembled both a delinquent version of Father and the Father we first met right after being summoned.”
“…I see, so that came up as well.”
“Is something the matter?”
“No, it’s nothing.”
Is this Ren’s own internal struggle? Father tilts his head in confusion.
“Ren, I was debating whether to bring this up, but would you like to hear how the Father from the first world and the one from the previous loop analyzed you?”
“Motoyasu-kun.”
Father gives me a warning look. I suppose I should stay quiet for now.
“Tell me. How did future Naofumi analyze me?”
“Ren…”
“Don’t look at me like that. To be honest, I’m not good with people like Naofumi.”
The mood in the room shifts instantly. Itsuki hesitates, unsure whether to speak.
“I have no intention of changing who I am. But I know that understanding something is different from being ignorant of it, so I want to hear it.”
“You won’t get mad?”
“Did my future self say something that bad?”
“Depends on how you take it.”

That’s what I think. If I recall correctly, the first world’s Father once said something about Ren’s sense of distance from his comrades during the Cal Mira Island incident. Something about how their formations functioned just fine even without Ren being there.
“Just tell me already.”
“The Father from the first world, before he had a change of heart, said that Ren’s behavior caused ‘coordination breakdowns typical of a misguided mentorship playstyle.’”
With just those words, Father seems to grasp how Ren operates.
“I see… Yeah, I do know someone who acts like that.”
“You’re wrong! All I did was teach my comrades the ways to get stronger when they asked me!”
“I get what you’re saying. Everyone has their own way of playing online games, so I’m not trying to force my perspective on you.”
Father speaks to Ren in a gentle tone.
“Ren, I have no intention of looking down on you. In fact, I appreciate that you’ve chosen to trust me. I want you to listen with that in mind.”
“I’m not here for a lecture.”
“And I don’t intend to give one. Maybe that’s how it was in the future Motoyasu knew, but things are different now. Ren, you’ve already taken a step forward.”
